name: Dermatofibroma
description: A dermatofibroma is a harmless, firm, small bump that usually forms on the arms or legs. It often feels like a hard little bead or pebble under the skin and may dimple inward when you pinch it from the sides.
common_symptoms: Small, firm bump (usually smaller than 1 centimeter)
Color can be pink, red, tan, light brown, or gray
Feels hard to the touch like a small pebble
Dimples downward into the skin when gently pinched (the 'dimple sign')
Commonly appears on lower legs or arms, sometimes after an insect bite
causes: An overgrowth of fibrous tissue in the skin dermis layer
Often triggered by a minor puncture injury, splinter, insect bite, or ingrown hair
risk_factors: More common in young and middle-aged adults
Slightly more frequent in women than men
History of insect bites or minor skin punctures
first_aid: Do not squeeze or attempt to puncture the nodule
Take care when shaving over the area so you do not nick it
precautions: Shave gently around the bump to prevent cuts and bleeding
Avoid repeatedly squeezing or pressing on the nodule
Notice if there are any changes in shape, size, or color
home_care: Keep the skin clean and moisturized
Cover with a small bandage if razor irritation occurs
do_not: DO NOT attempt to pop, cut, or squeeze the bump
DO NOT use over-the-counter boil or wart treatments on it
red_flags: The bump grows quickly in size beyond 1 to 2 centimeters
Persistent pain or severe burning sensation
when_to_see_doctor: See a doctor or healthcare provider if you have a new firm bump that grows, bleeds easily, hurts, or if you want confirmation of what the bump is.
prevention: Protect skin from insect bites with insect repellent
Avoid scratching minor puncture wounds or insect stings
